title: Access request categorization taxonomy and runtime routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of administration and access requests (RBAC role grants, SSO configuration changes, SCIM provisioning issues, org policy exceptions). The current intake flows conflate unrelated request types, causing long triage cycles, misrouted work, and occasional security exposures.

Goal: Define a clear, implementable taxonomy for admin/access requests and wire a runtime routing decision table that assigns incoming requests to the right queue (Self-serve docs, PM/Design, Security review, Dedicated SRE, Solutions Eng). The taxonomy should be lightweight, rule-driven, and extensible so it can be enforced by the intake UI and by automation (webhooks / classifier).

Success metrics: reduce average triage time from ~72 hours to <24 hours for enterprise admin requests; 30% fewer manually reassigned tickets; clearer SLA mapping for P1/P2 RBAC changes.
acceptance_criteria: A published taxonomy doc page with canonical categories, example requests, and routing destinations
An initial routing decision table (CSV) with top-level rules (e.g., change_type, scope, customer_tier, security_flag) that maps to destination queues
A prototype intake form schema (fields + validation rules) for RBAC/SSO/SCIM requests accepted by Support and Solutions Eng
Integration checklist for automating routing via existing intake API or webhook (owners identified)
Stakeholder sign-off from Security, Support, Solutions Eng, and two pilot enterprise customers
proposed_solution: Run discovery interviews with 8 enterprise customers + 5 internal operators to collect 100 representative request examples
Define 6 top-level categories: Role Management (RBAC), Identity Configuration (SSO/SAML), Provisioning (SCIM), Policy Exceptions, Org Structure Changes, Diagnostics/Incident follow-ups

Design a compact decision table with prioritized rules: if request contains 'SCIM' or 'provision' -> Provisioning queue; if request changes 'admin' role and affects >1 seat -> Security review + Dedicated SRE; else route to Support
Deliver a CSV routing table and an RFC for a webhook contract to accept 'category' and 'security_flags' from intake UI
Pilot the routing table with two enterprise customers for 4 weeks and measure misroutes and triage time
tradeoffs: Rule-based routing is easier to audit and implement quickly but will miss edge cases that an ML classifier could catch later
Tighter validation fields reduce noise but increase friction for customers—we will require minimum viable fields and progressive profiling
Automated routing reduces manual load but requires clear escalation paths to avoid misrouted security-sensitive changes being applied incorrectly
comments: 2025-02-11: Kickoff interview scheduling - 8 external customers agreed to 30-minute sessions (Mei + Diego leading).
2025-02-13: Security flagged 'admin role changes affecting >1 seat' as a high-risk pattern that must always require manual security review.
2025-02-15: Design uploaded intake form sketches (link above). Low-friction approach accepted: 3 required fields + optional attachments.
2025-02-18: Eng feasibility sync - Marcus confirmed intake-api can accept a 'category' field and evaluate routing rules server-side; ETA for POC webhook: 3 sprints.
2025-02-22: PM review - updated decision table to include 'customer_tier' and 'contracted_SLA' columns. Preparing pilot scope doc for two enterprise customers.
